root_cause_label: Unnecessary sed command removed LIMIT 500 from working solution; recovery attempts were error-prone and incomplete
one_sentence_failure_summary: After producing a correct and working optimized query in sol.sql (verified at steps 25-37), the agent made an unnecessary sed edit at step 42 that removed the LIMIT 500 clause, corrupting the previously correct solution, and though partial recovery was attempted the test still failed.
t_err_evidence: At step 40 the agent attempted a no-op str_replace (identical old_str and new_str), revealing it was starting unnecessary edits on a working solution; the harness returned an error saying the strings must differ, but the agent proceeded with further edits rather than stopping.
t_commit_evidence: At step 42, `sed -i '1d;$d'` deleted the first and last lines of sol.sql; as confirmed at step 43, this removed the LIMIT 500; clause from the query file, corrupting the previously working solution.
t_surface_evidence: At step 43, cat -n /app/sol.sql shows the file ends at line 46 (blank) with no LIMIT 500; clause visible, confirming the corruption introduced by step 42's sed command.
trigger_explanation: The agent falsely assumed the sol.sql file needed cosmetic cleanup (removing leading/trailing blank lines) even though the solution was already verified correct and working. Acting on this false premise led to the destructive sed command that removed LIMIT 500.
forewarning_evidence: Step 40's str_replace returned an error: 'No replacement was performed. new_str and old_str must be different.' This signaled that no changes were needed, but the agent ignored this and proceeded to apply sed edits in steps 41-42.
